content.description: Rig checks the application when the coding agent finishes its work. Findings go straight back to the agent, while the code and context are still fresh.

demo.label: Illustrative example: an agent adds a search endpoint, Rig confirms SQL injection, the agent parameterizes the query, and Rig retests it.

steps.title: The agent finishes a change. Rig starts a check.
steps.body: Rig connects to the agent’s completion hook. The check starts automatically, without a developer remembering to run a scan.

steps.title: Rig tests the running application.
steps.body: Rig runs the application locally and tracks how input moves through its code. It confirms a vulnerable execution path before reporting a finding.

steps.title: The agent gets evidence and fix instructions.
steps.body: Each finding identifies the code location, explains the vulnerability, and gives the agent guidance for fixing it. The same agent working on the feature can act on that feedback.

steps.title: Rig checks the updated code.
steps.body: After the agent makes a fix, Rig retests the reported vulnerability. The result shows whether the check passed, the issue remains, or testing could not complete.

content.intro: Static analysis finds potential vulnerabilities in source code. Rig adds evidence from the running application, separating what could happen from what happened during a test.

points.title: Reachability, confirmed.
points.body: Static analysis can identify a potentially vulnerable path. Rig confirms that the path actually executes in the running application before reporting a finding.

points.title: Runtime context, included.
points.body: Static analysis models how code may behave. Rig observes how it behaves with the inputs, configuration, and dependencies present during the test.

points.title: Evidence, ready to act on.
points.body: A static finding can leave developers checking whether an issue is reachable. Rig includes execution evidence and the code location, giving developers and agents concrete fix instructions.

glyph.label: Pixel glyph for the FAQ eyebrow

items.question: Does Rig work with my existing coding agents?
items.answer: Rig connects to a supported coding agent through its completion hook. During the demo, we’ll review the team’s agent and application to confirm fit.

items.question: Who makes the code changes / fixes to reported vulnerabilities?
items.answer: Your existing coding agent makes the fix. Rig supplies the finding, code location, and fix guidance, then checks the updated code.

items.question: Is Rig checking every keystroke?
items.answer: No. The automatic check starts when the agent signals that it has finished its work. Developers can also run a check manually through the CL

items.question: What happens if a fix does not work?
items.answer: Rig reports that the vulnerability remains. If testing cannot complete, that is reported separately from a passed check.

items.question: Does a clean scan mean the entire application is secure?
items.answer: No. It means Rig completed the checks within that scan’s scope without confirming a vulnerability. Untested paths are not proven safe, and incomplete checks are reported separately.

items.question: Will Rig Collect my Data?
items.answer: No, Rig is committed to being the most secure and private security testing tool available.. Our telemetry is limited. Tests run on device and code and conversations never leave the machine.
